clue.text: Foreign character thus created by John Milton senior

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a character from abroad
sic is Latin for thus, used to flag a quotation as printed

explanation.surface: A setter imagines some exotic figure invented by the poet's father.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet John Milton's father, also John, was a composer, so his creations were tunes rather than characters in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder Milton wrote madrigals and psalm settings, so what he composed was sound arranged for singers.

clue.text: Unusual ship's name is in bad form

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of the letters signals they are scrambled

parts.note: the word ship's, with its s counted as a letter

explanation.surface: An odd vessel's title is badly shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Misshapen means deformed or out of proportion, so its shape is poor.

clue.text: Do-gooder keeps a young chap endlessly in footwear

indicators.note: holding something within means the saint's letters go round the rest

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy do-gooder

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a boy is a young male

explanation.surface: A charitable person stores a lad's things in a shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: The do-gooder is a saint, abbreviated in the usual way; 'endlessly' docks the young chap's last letter and 'keeps' wraps the saint round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog worn by peasants in France, a kind of shoe.

clue.text: Acts that went against the grain, for some?

definitions.text: Acts that went against the grain, for some?

parts.words: Acts that went against the grain, for some?
parts.note: parliamentary acts that restricted imported cereal, unpopular with many who paid for bread

explanation.definitionFit: These nineteenth-century British statutes taxed imported cereal crops, so laws literally concerned grain.

clue.text: Naval man's gold concealed in a chest of drawers

definitions.note: read as 'naval man is', the 's standing for is

indicators.note: one item hidden inside another means the gold goes within the furniture

parts.note: a commode is an ornate chest of drawers
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A sailor's treasure is stashed away in a piece of bedroom furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A commodore is a naval officer ranking above captain, so the sailing officer is the man meant.

clue.text: Censor with the object of upholding accountant

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece holds up the other, sitting above it

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
to means in order to, with the aim of

explanation.surface: An official checker has a purpose in supporting the money man.
explanation.walkthrough: Cato the Elder held the office of censor in ancient Rome and was known simply as the Censor.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Elder was a Roman magistrate famous for his strict tenure as censor, overseeing public morals.

clue.text: Term for Moses and Elijah originally (Malachi's version)

indicators.note: a new version of the letters means they are rearranged
the opening letters of the two prophets' names are taken

parts.note: the word Malachi's with its s counted as a letter

explanation.surface: A biblical word for two prophets as rendered by a third.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes M and E; 'version' rearranges them with MALACHIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Michaelmas is the autumn session at Oxford, Cambridge and British schools, named after St Michael's feast.

clue.text: Presumably he's not even a weirdo

definitions.text: Presumably he's not even a weirdo

parts.words: Presumably he's not even a weirdo
parts.note: someone not even is odd in number, so an eccentric is jokingly someone not even

explanation.definitionFit: An oddity is an eccentric or strange person, someone peculiar.

clue.text: Subscribe too generously to the press

definitions.text: Subscribe too generously to the press

parts.words: Subscribe too generously to the press
parts.note: giving too many people to a throng, a press being a crowd of people

explanation.definitionFit: To pack an event beyond capacity is to fill it with too many people, oversubscribing it.

clue.text: One of Leonardo's school supporters

parts.note: a painter's stand, the sort used by artists of the school of Leonardo da Vinci

explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the wooden stand that holds a canvas upright while an artist paints.

clue.text: Cubic 25 shaped roughly like Iceland

indicators.note: giving the letters a rough new shape signals that they are rearranged

parts.note: 25 points to the answer at 25-down, a famous actor, which is a star

explanation.surface: Something cube-like is being likened, oddly, to the outline of a northern island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaped roughly' rearranges CUBIC plus STAR, the answer to 25-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland lies just south of the Arctic Circle, so its climate and position are just below the polar region.

clue.text: Deck ensemble

definitions.meaning: to deck is to adorn or clothe, as in decked out
an ensemble is an outfit, a set of clothes worn together

explanation.definitionFit: To deck someone is to clothe them finely, and an ensemble is a coordinated outfit or frock.

clue.text: They may cater for short vacations, half-term included

indicators.note: one thing taken inside another means the half word goes within the holidays

parts.note: hols is a British short form of holidays

indicators.note: taking half of the word term keeps only its first two letters

explanation.surface: Something provides for brief school breaks, with the mid-term holiday counted in.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-term is a British school's short mid-term holiday, which tempts the solver to read it whole; here it gives TE, half of 'term'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotels provide food and lodging, so they are businesses that supply meals and rooms to guests.

clue.text: Reportedly bad state of certain servicemen

indicators.note: a hint that the words should be heard as spoken, not spelt

parts.note: naughty means bad, and Cal is short for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Rumour has it some soldiers are in a sorry condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty Cal' (California being a state) said out loud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical describes sailors and ships, so it relates to seamen in the navy.

clue.text: Muscular opponent, but not against constitutional reform

indicators.note: reforming the make-up of the words means their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strong rival says he is not against changing the constitution.
explanation.definitionFit: An antagonist is a muscle that opposes another's action, and more widely an adversary.

clue.text: Plant identified by one member of the Pickwick Club

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
I is the Roman numeral one
Nathaniel Winkle is one of the club members in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers

explanation.surface: A flower is said to have been spotted by one of Dickens's comic club men.
explanation.walkthrough: Winkle, Snodgrass and Tupman are Mr Pickwick's companions in Dickens's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The periwinkle is a trailing evergreen with blue flowers, so it is a garden shrub.

clue.text: Taking a practical view about a Caliph's twitch

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Ali was the fourth caliph of Islam, with the 's giving S
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A sensible view on a Muslim ruler's nervous habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Being realistic means facing facts sensibly, so the view is pragmatic.

clue.text: One standing out as an employer

definitions.meaning: a raised knob or stud on a surface
the person in charge who pays the staff

explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a protruding ornament on a ceiling or shield, and also the manager who hires workers.

clue.text: King surrounded by cupbearers conversing in 28

definitions.note: points to the answer at 28-across; the plural here means charming types, wizards

indicators.note: the king's letters are placed within the other piece
in speech, so the word is as heard

parts.note: saucers bear cups
ER is short for Edward Rex, a king's title

explanation.surface: A monarch is ringed by royal servants chatting in a magical scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The cups' holders, spoken in a non-rhotic accent, sound like the start of the wizards' word; 'surrounded by' places the king's title inside, and 28 refers to the 28-across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard casts spells, so magicians are spellbinders of the kind 28 names.

clue.text: Jersey pattern? Just lies, it turns out

parts.note: fair means just

indicators.note: the word lies turned about becomes a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sweater design proves to be just untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it turns out' rearranges LIES to ISLE. A jersey is a British word for a knitted sweater; Fair Isle is a Scottish island famous for its colourful knitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair Isle is a style of multicoloured patterned knitting used for sweaters.

clue.text: A dextrous beast

definitions.meaning: deft or skilful with the hands
an old word for cattle or an ox

explanation.definitionFit: Neat means deft and adroit, and in old usage it names an ox or cow.

clue.text: Hot plate given by one girl to another, some say

indicators.note: signals that the letters are those of what is heard

parts.note: Sal, one girl's name, followed by Amanda, another

explanation.surface: Someone hands a heated dish from one young woman to her friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sal' then 'Amanda', spoken in a British accent that drops the final r, sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A salamander is a metal plate heated and held over food to brown it, a grill used in kitchens.

clue.text: Insect discovered about 100 AD, on April 1st

indicators.note: turned about means the word is read backwards

parts.note: I see, written IC, is the cry of someone who has found something out
C is the Roman numeral 100

indicators.note: the first letter of the month is taken

explanation.surface: A bug was found around the second century, on All Fools' Day.
explanation.definitionFit: The cicada is a large insect known for its loud shrill song in hot climates.

clue.text: Cooking utensil may be rigid, and not the reverse

indicators.note: the letters could be arranged another way, so they are mixed up
says the word for 'and not' is read backwards

parts.note: nor means and not

explanation.surface: A kitchen tool might be stiff, and not flexible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges RIGID to GRIDI; 'the reverse' turns NOR to RON.
explanation.definitionFit: A gridiron is a metal grill of parallel bars for broiling meat over a fire.

clue.text: Egyptian threat to shipping upended by diver

indicators.note: in a down entry the whole run is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for Egyptian
a berg is an iceberg, a hazard to ships

explanation.surface: A danger to vessels on the Nile is overturned by a swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grebes are waterbirds that dive underwater for fish.

clue.text: A right rogue, beginning to exploit the shopping mall!

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A scoundrel sets out to take advantage of a shopping centre.
explanation.definitionFit: An arcade is a covered walkway lined with shops, a kind of shopping precinct.

clue.text: Further article in a primitive engine

indicators.note: one piece going in another means the article sits within the machine

parts.note: a gin is an early machine, as in a cotton gin
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: More is written in a piece about an early machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Again can mean moreover or besides, adding a further point.

clue.text: Famous actor giving rise to an expression of disbelief

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: rats is an exclamation of scorn or disbelief

explanation.surface: A celebrated performer provokes a scornful cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a leading celebrity performer in films or theatre.

clue.text: Run more than is usual

definitions.meaning: in cricket an ... is a run not scored off the bat, such as a bye

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bye or wide is scored as a bonus run, and additional means beyond the normal.

clue.text: Lacking will to be among a number on trial, say

indicators.note: the solver is to say these words and hear the result

parts.note: in means among, test means trial, eight is a number

explanation.surface: Someone without a testament is one of several people facing a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In test eight' spoken quickly sounds like the answer; 'to be' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dies intestate leaves no legal testament disposing of their estate.

clue.text: Charming type of cockney bird — a singer…

parts.note: a hen with the h dropped, as a Londoner from the East End would say it
a chanter is one who chants or sings

explanation.surface: A delightful East End character is a songbird and vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the London East End accent, which drops the initial h, so hen becomes 'en.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchanter casts spells, so a charming type here is a wizard who bewitches.

clue.text: … but these are found in loftier nests

definitions.text: … but these are found in loftier nests

indicators.note: says the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: Continuing the bird theme from the clue before, some birds build their homes higher up.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 28's songbird; the eagles meant really do nest on high crags.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea eagles build eyries on cliffs and tall trees, so their homes are high up.
